title: Reactant
summary: A reactant is a substance that starts a chemical reaction — the material at the left side of a chemical equation that gets transformed. Hydrogen and oxygen are the reactants that combine to make water.

parts: Sits on the left of the equation
processes: Combining or breaking apart in a reaction
Being used up as the reaction proceeds
Reappearing as new substances — the products
plainLanguageExplanation: A reactant is a substance that takes part in a chemical reaction — it is the starting material, the ingredient. Picture making water: you start with hydrogen gas and oxygen gas. These two are the reactants. You put them together, a reaction happens, and they are transformed — you end with water. The reactants have been consumed, rearranged, and turned into something new. In a chemical equation, the reactants are always written on the LEFT side of the arrow: hydrogen + oxygen → water. The arrow means 'reacts to make.' Everything on the left is a reactant; everything on the right is a product. A key idea: reactants are not destroyed — they are rearranged. The same atoms that start on the left end up in the products, just connected differently. When you burn wood, oxygen is a reactant (along with the wood's carbon); when you cook food, the ingredients are the reactants; when you breathe, the glucose and oxygen in your cells are reactants. Every reaction starts with reactants and ends with products.

whyItMatters: Reactants are where every chemical change begins. Understanding what a reactant is — and how it is consumed and rearranged into products — is the first step to reading equations, predicting reactions, and understanding how matter transforms all around you.
didYouKnow: When you breathe out carbon dioxide, the reactants were glucose and oxygen inside your cells — and the carbon atoms in that breath were once part of your food.
compareReason: Reactant and product are the two ends of every reaction — comparing ingredients with the dish they produce makes the whole reaction concept concrete.
